method:rack::plugin::Model::appendContex.finding: P0 (found by reading the source, not run): append_context_menu can leave menu items that crash Rack. native/bindings/plugin.cpp:524 checks the model only with addedModel (plugin.cpp:214, which needs only m.plugin != NULL). It does not use committedModel (plugin.cpp:206), so a model attached to an isolated rp.Plugin() is accepted. Rack's Model::appendContextMenu (src/plugin/Model.cpp) adds items whose lambdas use `this` and read `plugin->...` when the item is chosen: the library item uses plugin->slug, and the favorite item calls isFavorite(), which uses plugin->slug. Plugin.close() (plugin.cpp:73) runs ~Plugin, which sets model->plugin = NULL (src/plugin/Plugin.cpp:14-18), and dropping the model afterwards deletes it. Rack's MenuItem::doAction (src/ui/MenuItem.cpp:86-93) does not check `disabled`. So these steps dereference NULL or freed memory: append_context_menu(menu), then plugin.close() (and optionally del model), then choose an item by clicking or with do_action. This is the dangling-raw-Model* hazard that RP-31M closed for create_module and create_module_widget. Separately (P2), the cited anchor docs/reference/plugin.md#plugin-models does not mention append_context_menu or in_browser; it is described in docs/reference/ui.md:119. Smallest fix: use committedModel(h, "Model.append_context_menu") and add a test that a detached or isolated model is refused. Cite ui.md#ui-menu-helpers, or document the method and in_browser under #plugin-models.
